# KS-1036 — Wednesday's task for Ornith, checklist item 3 only, **DOCUMENTATION (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md`, no code)** — **r1, THE ONE REBRIEF** under Kam's 2026-09-16 counter (original + one rebrief, then a Claude agent). The original is kept beside this file as `KS-1036.md.pre-0916-r1`. Written 2026-09-16 21:5x from the file at develop `0b25f823f` (0 files under `Blockchain/Dev` differ from `48e65c435`, where the original was written).

**Why r1 exists (read it, then do the task):** round 1 wrote every new line word-for-word right, but put them after a DIFFERENT paragraph, about ten lines further down the file, in the next section. This time the new lines are appended to ONE named paragraph, directly under its last line `their stream.`, with no blank line between — the only place in the file where that line exists.

## What to change (one paragraph)

`DEV-PROCESS.md:212-215` says "All **97** active Platform K tickets now sit under four parents — 40 +
19 + 18 + 20, nothing left over". That was the 2026-09-03 snapshot; it has decayed. KS-1036 item 3 asks
to correct the counts "or, better, stop hardcoding a number that decays and point at a query". This task
keeps the historical sentence (it records what Kam adopted on 09-03) and appends six dated lines to the
END of the section's LAST paragraph (`:224-227`, the paragraph that says every new ticket
is parented into one of the four): the figures are a snapshot, what they measure today, and how to count
instead. Nothing existing changes. Items 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the ticket are NOT this task.

## Where

- `:212-215` — (correct, historical) the 09-03 sentence with 97 and 40 + 19 + 18 + 20. NOT touched.
- `:224-227` — (correct) the paragraph that begins `The 18 catalogue projects are unchanged` and ends on its own short line.
- `:226` — (correct) `parented into one of the four** (or into a new stream, proposed first). A wrap that files tickets names` — stays.
- `:227` — (correct) `their stream.` — thirteen characters, the paragraph's last line, the only line in the file that is exactly this. Stays; the new lines go directly after it, with NO blank line between.
- `:228` — (correct) a blank line. Stays, directly below the new lines.

## The exact change — ONE INSERT-ONLY hunk, 6 new lines

Insert AFTER line 227 (`their stream.`) and BEFORE line 228 (the blank line).

The six new lines CONTINUE the paragraph that ends at line 227: none of them is blank, none starts with
`>` or `-` or `#`, and each starts at column 0 (in the diff: `+` immediately followed by the first word).
The fence below holds ONLY the added lines, each with a leading `+`. Copy every `+` line character for
character, including the two asterisks at each end of the bold sentence and the straight double quotes.
No `+` line contains a dollar sign, a backslash, an em dash or a backtick.

```
+**Measured 2026-09-16 (KS-1036): the counts above are the 2026-09-03 snapshot and have decayed.**
+Of the 71 KS tickets in a started or unstarted state, 40 sit directly under one of the four
+parents (KS-485 9, KS-770 10, KS-771 9, KS-772 12), 2 under another parent and 29 under none.
+Do not quote 97 or "nothing left over" as current. When the number matters, count it at the time:
+the direct children of KS-485, KS-770, KS-771 and KS-772 that are started or unstarted, against
+every started or unstarted ticket on team KS.
```

The hunk's context is TWO lines above and ONE line below, copied from `files[...]`: above, line 226 and
line 227 (` their stream.` as a diff context line); below, line 228 (blank — a single space as a diff
context line). Do NOT touch lines 210-228; do NOT re-flow line 227 into the new lines; do NOT add a blank
line.

## Required (the checker's proof — each token ABSENT in the section before, PRESENT after)
- `### The four review streams` :: KS-1036, decayed, snapshot

## Premises (measured)

- **The file at the tip, and the anchor.** Instrument: `git show 0b25f823f:Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` into python (2026-09-16 21:5x): 267 lines; `:227` equals `their stream.` and occurs exactly once; `:226` occurs exactly once; `:228` is blank. `git diff --stat 48e65c435 0b25f823f -- Blockchain/Dev` → empty.
- **The doc states 97 and 40 + 19 + 18 + 20, "nothing left over".** Instrument: `:212-215` read at `0b25f823f`.
- **The section and the tokens.** Instrument: the section `### The four review streams, built 2026-09-03` runs `:210` to the next heading of level ≤ 3 (the checker's `###` rule), i.e. `:210-228`; the checker's token regex over those lines → `KS-1036` 0, `decayed` 0, `snapshot` 0 (and 0 in the whole file).
- **71 started-or-unstarted KS tickets; 40 directly under the four parents; 2 under another parent; 29 with none.** Instrument, CARRIED from the original commission (not re-measured by this rebrief — no Linear read from here): Linear GraphQL at 2026-09-16 21:2x, `issues(filter:{team:{key:{eq:"KS"}}, state:{type:{in:["started","unstarted"]}}})` paginated 100 at a time, `parent{identifier}` tallied; cross-check from each parent's `children(first:250)` filtered to started/unstarted → KS-485 9, KS-770 10, KS-771 9, KS-772 12 = 40; control: with `backlog` added the same query returns 356 tickets and 47 under the four, so the state filter discriminates. These figures move with the board: re-measure at raise time.
- **The checker passes THIS shape and refuses round 1's.** Instrument: the real `tasks/doc_patch/checker.sh` in a scratch clone at `0b25f823f` against the input built from this brief (21:5x): the intended hunk → PASS (8/8), D2 strict, with context 2 above / 1 below, 1 / 1 and 3 / 3; round 1's actual `out.md` → FAIL (4) D5+D6+D8+D9; the six lines at round 1's position → FAIL (3) D5+D6+D9; the six lines one line low (after the blank `:228`) → FAIL (1) D9; line 227 re-flowed into the first new line → FAIL (2) D8+D9.

## Output

Exactly ONE ```diff block, ONE file section `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` /
`+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md`, ONE hunk `@@ -226,3 +226,9 @@`: context lines 226 and 227,
the six `+` lines exactly as above, and the blank context line 228.

## Notes for the raise (not for the model)

- **Shape changed from the original** (see `KS-1036.md.pre-0916-r1`): a separate blockquote became the
  closing sentences of the section's last paragraph, so the edit needs no blank `+` line at all. Same facts,
  same words, without the `> ` prefix. If the model adds a trailing blank `+` line out of habit, the file
  gets a harmless double blank before the next heading (measured: still PASS) — tidy it at raise.
- **Partial by design:** item 3 only. The board work (items 1-2), the KS-485 rename (item 4, already met by
  the table) and the check's home (item 5, a decision) stay open.
- The figures are dated; re-measure at raise time with the query in Premises and update the one line if
  they moved.
- Not asserted: whether the review-stream overlay is still in force after the 2026-09-11 approval ruling,
  and whether the 29 unparented tickets breach the "reaches Todo" rule. Both are the reviewer's.

# Secuura development process

**Agreed 25 August 2026 — Stuart, Peter, Kamil.**

Five stages, two roles. Authors test their own work and record it in the PR; the PR is TESTED (as defined in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, step 6 of *Adopted merge flow*) and Wednesday's GO, naming the head SHA, approves it (Kam, 2026-09-11); the author merges and deploys. Deploys stay manual, so no CI/CD minutes are billed.

## The flow

```
  01 ─────────── 02 ─────────── 03 ─────────── 04 ─────────── 05
  Author         Author         QA gate        Author         Author
  Build on       Test it,       Verdict &      Merge to       Pull and
  a branch       raise PR       Wednesday GO   develop        deploy
```

| # | Owner | Stage | What happens |
|---|-------|-------|--------------|
| 01 | Author | Build on a branch | Develop on a feature branch off `develop`. Commit and push as you go. **Name the branch after your own work, never after someone else's ticket** — the Linear/GitHub integration moves a ticket to *In Progress* the moment a branch or PR carries its key, and on 26 Aug that silently moved a ticket Stuart owns. |
| 02 | Author | Test it, then raise the PR | Test your own work before the PR goes up and fill in the **Test Evidence** block (below) in the description: what you touched, what you ran, what you didn't get to, any migrations or config changes. Short is fine; honest is required — a "not run" line is the point of the block, because the QA gate reads it and needs to know where to look. **The four platform suites are the author's final check before handover** — see below. |
| 03 | QA gate | Verdict & Wednesday GO | A QA gate verdict — GO or GO WITH FINDINGS — at the PR's **current head**, then **Wednesday's GO, which names the head SHA and is the approval** (Kam, 2026-09-11: *"For the time being, I / you will approve our own elements"*). Peter runs periodic formal test passes on top; demo (UAT) is updated only after his nod. |
| 04 | Author | Merge to develop | The author merges once the PR is **TESTED** and has **Wednesday's GO** — and, when GitHub Actions is available, checks are green. `develop` never waits on one person being at their desk. Squash-merge preferred. |
| 05 | Author | Pull and deploy | Pull `develop` and run the deploy manually. Whoever merged deploys, verifies at the target (not just locally — demo runs real anchoring where local mocks it), and stays on hand if it goes bang — demo (UAT) only after Peter's nod. |

## The four platform suites are the final check (Kam, 2026-08-27)

> **These four run as the author's FINAL CHECK before the PR is handed to review; the reviewer red-pens the results (Kam, 2026-08-27).**

Ruled verbatim: *"So we run with the tests and add to the pr and then Peter checks our results with his red pen. Yes, please make it a process rule and always run as a final check."*

They run **locally** — see [Manual CI-gate equivalents](#manual-ci-gate-equivalents) for the command, pass criterion and wall-clock of each. A suite you did not run is a `not run + why` line, not a blank and not a ticked box.

## Test Evidence block (paste into every PR description)

```markdown
## Test Evidence
- **Touched:** which services / packages / files
- **Ran:** which suites actually executed, and their results
- **NOT run:** what you did not get to, and why
- **Migrations / config:** any schema change, env var, or config this needs

### Platform suites — final check (Kam's rule 2026-08-27)
- **Schemathesis:** run/result — **the failing SET (operation ids) + its diff vs the develop baseline set**, never a bare count | not run + why
- **Akto:** run/result | not run + why
- **Playwright:** run/result | not run + why
- **Performance / k6:** run/result | not run + why
- **Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why
- **Cross-cutting guards (`packages/shared`):** run/result | not run + why
```

**Why cross-cutting guards get their own line.** They live in `packages/shared` but assert
things about **every service** — today `crypto-agility.guard` and
`ks727-errorhandler-class-guard`, which walks the whole tree, imports every exported
`errorHandler` and drives it through a real route. Under "run `npm test` in the touched
service" they execute only when someone touches `shared`, which is the change least likely
to add a fifteenth service error handler. A guard on no path that runs is not a guard, so
it is named here separately and run on **any** service change.

This is the wording already in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md) (merged as PR #733), so the two documents say the same thing.

**A line must say what happened, not what applies.** "Run and passing" means a run whose result you read. If a suite has no bearing on the change, write `not run — no spec change, no new route or method`; do not tick it as done. A box ticked on a not-applicable rationale reads to the reviewer as a run, and at least one open PR (#686) had exactly that.

## Why it's shaped this way

- **Review isn't testing.** Untested PRs turn the reviewer into the bottleneck and stall the automation work Peter owns.
- **Separate the ticket from the review.** The author tests, but a second pair of eyes signs it off — never the same person on both.
- **Merging doesn't wait on the reviewer.** Approval is the gate, not availability. `develop` keeps moving when someone is off.
- **Manual deploys, no billed minutes.** The reason the last stage is by hand rather than a pipeline.

## GitHub Actions is retired for this repository (Kam, 2026-08-27)

Actions stopped starting jobs on 17 August on org billing. On **27 August Kam decided not to restore it** — verbatim: *"billing will not be fixed. Please find and use a workaround (this new process) going forward."* So this is a **decided state, not an outage**: there is nothing to wait for and no leg that re-arms by itself.

- **The gate is: a PR that is TESTED (as defined in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, step 6 of *Adopted merge flow*), with its Test Evidence block's four platform-suite lines and unit-suite line filled from LOCAL runs** under `systemTest/` and the services' own test runners, **plus Wednesday's GO naming the head SHA** (Kam, 2026-09-11).
- **`mergeable_state: clean` is not evidence that anything was tested.** GitHub reporting a PR as *clean* means only that no required check is currently failing or pending. **It does not mean a check ran.** With no checks running at all, every PR reads *clean* or *unstable* for reasons unrelated to whether the code works. The Test Evidence block carries the testing claim; the GitHub badge carries none of it. (KS-660 / PR #721 exist to bannerise exactly this.)
- **The frozen-queue ordering that waited on Actions returning no longer applies.** The queue moves on approval + local evidence like any other PR. Dependabot PRs (15 waiting) follow the same five stages; batch them.

## Manual CI-gate equivalents

Every job that used to gate a PR, and the local command that now stands in for it. **This is the mapping KS-685 commissioned.** Run from the repo root unless a working directory is given.

Prerequisites for anything that scans a running system: Docker Desktop up and the platform stack answering on `http://localhost:6882`. Akto additionally needs its **own** second compose stack — a one-time `npm run start` in `systemTest/akto`.

### ⚠ Read this before you trust a red — four ways these runs lie

The first three were hit on the **first** run under this rule (2026-08-27); the fourth on the second night. None is hypothetical.

**1. A partial stack produces a confident FALSE RED.** `docker-compose.local.yml` defines **38 services**. If some are down, the gateway answers `502 BAD_GATEWAY — Upstream service "X" is unreachable` and the suites record it as a failure indistinguishable from a real defect. The first Schemathesis sweep of the day returned **14 failures that were entirely this** — 18 of 38 services were up, and the six named in the 502s were simply not running. Starting them (from existing images, ~2 s, no rebuild) turned all five probed endpoints from `502` into `401`.

> **Before any suite run:** `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml ps` and confirm every service is up.
> **`502 BAD_GATEWAY` in a result means a missing service, not a bug.** Never file a regression off one.

**2. The pre-merge sweep poisons its own next run.** The fuzz tiers change the test persona's password, so a **second** back-to-back run fails at *setup* with `401 Unauthorized` on `/api/auth/login` — **378 failures, every one of them setup, zero of them findings.** The `Run validity: OK — 0 of N operations errored` line does **not** catch this: it counts schemathesis operations, not pytest setup errors, so an entirely invalid run still self-reports as valid.

> **Between pre-merge runs:** `docker restart secuura-auth` (re-seeds the personas' CREDENTIALS AND ACCOUNT
> STATE — password, role, verification level, status, emailVerified, tenant; ~25 s). It does **not** restore
> anything else: when the row already exists the seeder writes exactly those fields and returns
> (`userRepo.ts:1475`), so profile fields a fuzz run mutated survive the restart.
> Distinguishing signature — check `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'lockout:*'` first. **Zero lockout keys + a healthy login for a known-good account = changed persona password, not a lockout.**

**3. The k6 gate exits 0 on a red.** Pointed at a dead port, the gate printed `Passed: 3/5 — 2 GATE(S) FAILED ✗` and **exited 0**; the runner separately prints `advisory scenario (blocking: false), not failing the run`. So `npm run test:smoke` returns success on a failing smoke.

> **Read the printed `Status:` line. Never read `$?` for this suite.** Anything that scripts around the exit code gets a silent false green — the same failure class as treating `mergeable_state: clean` as tested.

**4. A failure COUNT is not a signature — the failing SET is.** Schemathesis discovers a deterministic defect stochastically: Hypothesis has to generate a body that both clears validation and carries the offending value, so the same code returns a different failing set from run to run. Three `pr` runs on the same base commit on 2026-08-27:

| run | count | failing set |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `pr-…T10-12-12Z` | 9 | the KS-693 floor |
| `pr-…T10-29-58Z` | 10 | floor **+ `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody`** — the run that found KS-697 |
| `pr-…T11-04-05Z` | 10 | floor **− transfer-custody + `POST /api/security/rate-limit/check`** — the run that found KS-698 |

The last two are both "10". Read as a count that says *unchanged*, and it would have been wrong twice in one number: it hid a **fix landing** and a **new security defect arriving** simultaneously. "FAIL 9, byte-identical to baseline" was the phrasing used on several PRs that day, and it was a weaker claim than it reads.

> **Every Test Evidence block records the failing SET — the operation ids — and its diff against the current `develop` baseline set. Never a bare `FAIL N`.**
> Extract it from the run's `schemathesis-output.xml` (one `<testcase>` per operation; the failing ones carry a `<failure>`), or from the HTML report. A set that matches the baseline exactly is the only thing that earns the words *no new failures*.
> **The absence of an operation is not proof it is fixed**, and its presence is not proof it is new — a stochastic finder can miss a live defect on any given run. Absence is evidence only against a baseline set gathered the same way.

**Akto cannot do this yet, and that is a known gap.** Its findings arrive with no captured request (KS-696), so its failing set cannot be re-derived by hand or diffed with confidence — and its rich capture can fail silently and report zeros it never measured (KS-700). Until both are closed, read an Akto **PASS** as *nothing was reported*, not as *nothing is there*.

| Former CI job | Workflow it lived in | Local runner | Command | Pass criterion | Wall-clock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Schemathesis suite** | `pr-platform-suites.yml` | `systemTest/schemathesis` | `python3 scripts/run.py pr --base-url http://localhost:6882` | zero failures | **1.4 min measured** (1,554 cases over 307 ops) |
| **Schemathesis pre-merge sweep** | `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` | `systemTest/schemathesis` | `python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge --base-url http://localhost:6882` | zero failures | **13.4 min measured** (2026-08-27, 12 workers, ~2,016 cases over 318 ops). The runner's own docs say ~6.5 min — that is roughly half the real figure on a dev Mac. |
| **Spec-auth conformance (KS-380)** | `pr-platform-suites.yml`, inside the Schemathesis job | `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight` | `node scripts/preflight/spec-auth-conformance.mjs --base http://localhost:6882` | every bearer-authed op rejects unauthenticated | seconds |
| **Playwright suite** | `pr-platform-suites.yml` | `systemTest/playwright` | `npm run quality:static && npm run test:unit && npm run test:e2e` | all three pass | **3.8 s measured** — see the caveat below the table |
| **Performance suite (k6 smoke)** | `pr-platform-suites.yml` | `systemTest/performance` | `cp config/secrets.example.yml config/secrets.yml` (first time), then `npm run test:smoke` | **the printed `Status:` line must read ALL GATES PASSED — NOT the exit code, which is 0 either way (trap 3)** | **53 s measured** |
| **Akto suite (PR)** | `pr-platform-suites.yml` | `systemTest/akto` | `npm run start` (one-time), then `npm run test:pr` | BOLA / BFLA / Broken-Auth scan clean | ~7–8 min |
| **Akto pre-merge (full)** | `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml` | `systemTest/akto` | `npm run start` (one-time), then `npm run test:pre-merge` | as above, plus SM | ~7–8 min (full OWASP ~30–50 min) |
| **Shell suites** | `pr-platform-suites.yml` and `nightly-platform-suites.yml` (a `run:` step in each, never a required check) | repo root, or `Blockchain/Dev` | **Preflight leg 14 runs them on every push.** On demand: `npm run test:shell`, or `bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh --list` to see what is reached | every suite green; the runner refuses an empty run rather than reporting one | **38–39 s measured** (2026-09-04, 10 suites, two runs) |
| **Code Security Gates** | `pr-security-gates.yml` | `Blockchain/Dev` | `bash scripts/check-production-guard.sh` · `node tests/connectors/check-coverage.mjs` · `bash scripts/security-audit.sh` · `bash scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh` · `bash scripts/check-connector-xss.sh` | every script exits 0 | seconds each |
| **PR — Lockfiles** (clean-room `npm ci`) | `pr-lockfiles.yml` | `Blockchain/Dev` | `bash scripts/preflight/lockfile-cleanroom.sh` | clean-room install succeeds for every standalone lock | minutes |
| **Migration behaviour (KS-667)** | ***never had a CI job*** — added with the scenarios themselves | `Blockchain/Dev` | `npm run test:migrations` | all five scenarios `ok`; a failed scenario is a **non-zero exit**, not green text | ~40 s (spins a throwaway `postgres:15`, `trap cleanup EXIT`) |
| **Services' unit suites** | ***never had a CI job*** — KS-634 | each touched service | `npm test` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/<service>` (25 services carry a `test` script; `npm test --workspaces` runs all) | all pass | per service |
| **Cross-cutting guards** (`packages/shared`) | ***never had a CI job*** — KS-634 / KS-727 | `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared` | `npm test -w packages/shared` — run on **ANY service change**, not only a change to `shared` | all pass | seconds |
| **Nightly Internal Audit** | `internal-audit.yml` | *no local equivalent yet* | — | — | tracked as a new Low ticket; not built |

**Akto figures are unbaselined on this hardware (KS-691, 2026-09-01).** A PR-tier scan measured **24.7 s** and a pre-merge tier **30.2 s** on an 8-CPU Mac — against the ~7–8 min in the table above. That run was contended (four platform slots, 132 containers, two scans concurrent), so it is *not* offered as a replacement budget; a contended run should be slower, not two orders of magnitude faster, which is what makes the gap worth resolving rather than ignoring. Treat the table's Akto rows as inherited from another host until someone measures them uncontended here.

**Playwright, measured — and the number is itself the finding.** The suite is **12 tests in 4 files, 3.8 seconds**, across two projects (`auth-setup`, `api`). The retired CI job capped it at **40 minutes**; the real suite runs four orders of magnitude under that, so the cap never told anyone anything.

⚠ **Despite the name, this suite drives no browser.** Both projects are API-level — there is no UI or journey tier. Read a green here as *"12 API assertions passed"*, not as *"the portals work"*. The CI job name *Playwright suite* implies coverage this suite does not have.

**Do not dispatch `pre-merge-platform-suites.yml`** — the workflow is under a standing do-not-dispatch instruction (KS-441) and, with Actions retired, dispatching it cannot produce a result anyway. Run the local equivalent above.

### Known frictions

- The schemathesis **lint gate** is bound to the machine its venv was built on; the suite itself runs anywhere the venv resolves. Run the suite, skip the lint gate, and say so in the evidence block.
- Repeated auth-heavy runs trip the login limiter. Set `LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED=true` for back-to-back runs.
- The pre-merge fuzz tiers change the demo user's password, which breaks the push preflight afterwards. `docker restart secuura-auth` re-seeds it.

## Work is organised by stream, not by ticket (Kam, 2026-09-02)

**Agreed out of the 2026-09-02 catch-up.** Kam's words, verbatim: *"it would help Peter if we aggregated PRs
and things into projects. So if multiple items relate to the same stream, let's start creating projects and
groups so that multiple tickets can aggregate into one project. That way, Peter can run a test on one stream
rather than a dozen different streams… Create this as a policy for Secuura ongoing because this is the new
way we want to interact with Peter."*

This sits alongside the five stages above; it does not replace them. Nothing here changes what approval
means or who merges.

### 1. Every ticket belongs to exactly one stream

A **stream** is a Linear project. Every open ticket — backlog and active — carries one. A ticket with no
stream is a triage question, not a stream of its own, and gets one at the next sweep. New tickets are filed
inside a stream.

The seed streams came from Kam directly: **Connectors** (Outlook and every other connector — Stuart leads
Platform S and connectors now, and Platform K no longer builds them) and **Commercialisation** (key
rotation, chain changes, anything that only matters at commercial launch). The rest were derived from the
board's own text at the 2026-09-02 pass and are listed in
[`BOARD-CATALOGUE-2026-09-02.md`](./BOARD-CATALOGUE-2026-09-02.md).

### 2. Peter is handed a stream, not a ticket

- Tickets in a stream are built and handed over **together**, with **one evidence set** — the four platform
  suites plus the change's own e2e project — posted on the **project**, not repeated on every ticket.
- Peter runs **one test pass per stream** and makes **one approval decision per stream**.
- **A single-ticket stream is still a stream.** Unrelated work is not batched to look tidy, and related work
  is not split to look small.
- PR granularity stays with the author: one stream does not have to mean one PR. What must be true is that
  the stream's evidence is in one place and Peter tests it once.
- Ticket comments point at the project rather than restating its evidence.

Hold classes are unchanged. Nothing merges until it is TESTED (as defined in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, step 6 of
*Adopted merge flow*) and Wednesday's GO names the head SHA (Kam, 2026-09-11). Where a GitHub approval exists, it is read from the
reviews endpoint (`commit_id == head.sha`) — the GitHub **search index cannot see approval staleness** and
will list a PR as approved when its only approval is many commits back. A reviewer's own PRs are theirs to
merge.

### 3. Parked work is ARCHIVED, never closed

Each ticket carries one of three dispositions, read from its **description** rather than its title — a
title says what a ticket is about, only the description says whether it can be acted on:

| disposition | meaning | where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| **Action** | actionable now, needs nobody outside the team | the standing queue |
| **Escalate** | needs Kam's ruling, or Stuart / Peter / Phil | a dated card with a default |
| **Archive for now** | back-burner or not-yet-possible | **archived, not closed** |

Kam, 2026-09-02: *"don't close them, just archive them."* Linear unarchives, so an archived ticket is one
click from returning — and because it is archived **inside its stream project**, a whole stream comes back
as a set. **"Closed as not planned" is not used**; archived-not-closed is the only parking state.

This also keeps the Linear active-issue cap spent on work that can actually move. The cap refuses
`issueCreate` workspace-wide; it does **not** block `projectCreate`, `issueUpdate(projectId)` or
`issueArchive` — all three were measured on 2026-09-02 and work.

## Review capacity — the constraint this flow creates

On 26 Aug, **16 of our open PRs carry zero approvals**, and Peter has moved onto Platform S. A flow where every merge waits on one reviewer's approval moves the bottleneck from CI to that reviewer. Two things keep `develop` moving:

1. **Approval can come from any of the three who is not the author** — Stuart, Peter or Kamil. The rule is *not the same person*, not *always Peter*. Peter remains the default for auth, tenancy, migrations and cross-service changes.
2. **Authors make review cheap:** small PRs, the Test Evidence block filled in, and the "NOT run" lines honest so the reviewer's sample testing lands where it matters.
